name: a test widget for sweep coverage
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

a test widget for sweep coverage

phase_0.boundary_condition: the sealed coverage panel that holds the matrix, the heatmap render, and the appended log for one sweep run
phase_0.domain_name: a test widget for sweep coverage
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: sweep pointer advancing to the next parameter cell
AFWD.justification: the widget moves the test forward across frequency, amplitude, and input size axes

AREV.chosen_element: pointer stepping back to a missed cell for repeat
AREV.justification: the widget descends to an earlier grid position when a probe reports a gap

CLINK.chosen_element: chain from parameter selection to execution to probe capture
CLINK.justification: three stages link in order so each selected cell produces a measured hit count

ENGAGR.chosen_element: flaky cell showing hit on one repeat and miss on another
ENGAGR.justification: the same grid position holds both outcomes across repeats without discarding either

EVALF.justification: the probe marks that the sweep left the line unreached under the current parameters

EVALT.justification: the probe affirms that the sweep reached the line under the current parameters

FFUSE.chosen_element: hit tally and miss tally merging into one matrix
FFUSE.justification: the two arms rejoin into a single grid where each cell carries its combined count

FSPLIT.chosen_element: execution path dividing into hit arm and miss arm
FSPLIT.justification: one probe stream divides into cells that recorded a hit and cells that recorded no hit

IFIX.chosen_element: append only log of sweep cycles and matrix snapshots
IFIX.justification: each completed cycle is written to permanent storage that the widget cannot edit or erase

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: widget header showing its own sweep identifier
IMSCRIB.justification: the widget names itself in the display so the matrix is traced to its source run

TANCH.chosen_element: closed coverage panel presented for review
TANCH.justification: the panel encloses the final matrix and heatmap and stops further counting for the run

VINIT.chosen_element: empty widget shell with no grid loaded
VINIT.justification: the sweep has no parameters, no targets, and no counts before configuration arrives

phase_2.fuse_element: hit tally and miss tally merging into one matrix
phase_2.fuse_result: unified coverage matrix with per cell hit counts and gap flags
phase_2.rejoin_note: the hit arm increments counters and paints covered cells while the miss arm queues gaps for repeat, then both arms rejoin into the shared matrix
phase_2.split_element: execution path dividing into hit arm and miss arm
phase_2.split_input: completed probe capture for the current sweep cell
split_outputs: miss arm queuing uncovered lines for retry
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) both held at once: flaky cell recorded hit and miss across repeats
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) constructively refuted: probe marked a miss for the cell
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) constructively proven: probe affirmed a hit for the cell
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) neither: widget empty with no sweep defined and no counts established

steps.domain_action: empty widget shell awaits sweep definition
load parameter grid and target source files
chain parameter selection to test execution to probe capture
divide probe stream into hit arm and miss arm
probe records hit on instrumented line
increment hit counter and mark cell covered
probe records miss on instrumented line
step sweep pointer back to missed cell for retry
merge hit tally and miss tally into unified coverage matrix
hold flaky cell that hit once and missed once across repeats
chain matrix update to heatmap render
display widget sweep identifier in panel header
append sweep cycle and matrix snapshot to permanent log
seal coverage panel and present matrix for review

phase_5.alfs_store: bootstrap store holding default grids, probe maps, and prior coverage baselines
phase_5.compiler_frontend: sweep definition parser that turns grid ranges and target paths into executable test calls
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: event bus carrying parameter selections from controls to runner and probe counts back to matrix
phase_5.memory_mechanism: in memory grid store for live counts backed by snapshot files for prior cycles
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: round robin sweep driver that orders cell visits and inserts retries for missed cells

phase_6.cycle_cost: one test execution plus probe capture and matrix write per grid cell
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS approx 0 - the cycle trades execution time for stored counts with no residual queue
phase_6.post_cycle_state: matrix filled with hit counts, heatmap painted, and log extended by one snapshot
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: grid defined with counters at zero and no heatmap painted
